review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Hardware versus software client/server meanings; file and database services; Jenkins and software automation; browser and HTTP intermediary roles; caches and client-server design.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. IETF, MDN, PostgreSQL, Samba, Jenkins and Fielding support technical extensions. Source prose and code are not copied; qualified labels and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U3 with unspecified strength. Existing home contexts and valid direct genera remain unchanged. Client and server are roles in an interaction, not mutually exclusive kinds of program. Generic service requests may use local IPC; their network-specific children remain narrower.

sense_decisions.scope: Processing a request to a software service, including local interprocess communication.
Sending a request to a software service; a physical network is not required.
Software providing a service to requesting client software; distinguish it from the host hardware.
Software requesting another service in a particular interaction; it can also serve other clients.
Software serving database operations requested by clients, distinct from the database data and its physical host.
A client program making requests to a database service; it may run on the same machine.
A physical server used to provide shared file access; distinguish it from the serving program.
Software providing access to files through a service.
Providing network clients with access to files; not a physical serving utensil or merely storing a file.
The existing hardware genus matches the physical-server sense; do not import the waiter, sports player or utensil senses.
The dictionary definition includes any network-connected computer. Client role requires requesting a service; do not equate all network hosts with clients.
Retain workstation as a computer kind without importing the historic microcomputer performance comparison.
Software intended to automate tasks, distinct from the automation process itself.
Server software intended to coordinate automated tasks.
Automation directed at the named development activity; distinguish it from every manual or automated execution of that activity.
Automation directed at the named development activity; distinguish it from every manual or automated execution of that activity.
Automation directed at the named development activity; distinguish it from every manual or automated execution of that activity.
An initiating HTTP client role; live human interaction is not required.
An application for retrieving and presenting web pages; not a casual human shopper.
An automated user agent traversing web resources through HTTP; it need not build a search-engine index.
Software able to originate authoritative responses for its target resources.
An active HTTP message intermediary using HTTP on both sides, with distinct connection roles.
The client-selected HTTP message-forwarding proxy role.
An HTTP-facing gateway whose backend protocol need not be HTTP.
A reverse proxy specifically using HTTP on both sides.
The software subsystem managing reusable HTTP responses; distinguish it from the stored response data and hardware memory.
A cache component dedicated to one user; private does not mean cryptographically protected or secret.
A cache component supporting reuse across multiple users.
Managing storage and reuse of eligible HTTP responses under the protocol rules.
Software incorporating an HTTP response cache, without imposing a client-only or server-only role.
A forward proxy specifically incorporating a shared HTTP cache.
The software design style separating requesting clients and service providers.
A software architecture conforming to the client-server style, distinct from the style itself.
Preserve the broader software tree, including inherited repository/tool and development-result claims still awaiting review.
Database data, DBMS products, database systems and keys require a dedicated review before changing their old children.
The broad computer record remains under home appliances; do not propagate that narrow household genus into every new technical role.
Pipeline is polysemous across a workflow description, execution and processor design. Do not identify it with Jenkins Pipeline without reviewing the original sense.
Preserve software architecture; its Dataflow Programming child needs a separate paradigm review.
Preserve existing deployment/release chronology and outcome rows pending a lifecycle review.
Reuse the physical network-host family; virtual host and virtual machine meanings need separate records.

review.limits: No deployment, network service, scraper or test suite is executed. No product-version, performance or security guarantee is encoded. A reverse proxy may use a non-HTTP backend; only an explicitly HTTP-to-HTTP subtype receives both HTTP endpoint genera. Caching is optional, and private does not mean secret. General computer/home-appliance ancestry, database/DBMS/SQLite/foreign-key distinctions, dataflow, Pipeline, protocol/standard links and inherited lifecycle probabilities remain queued.

exclusion_review.decision: Preserve zero shared-descendant exclusion candidates in both contexts. Client/server program roles may overlap; no global disjointness assertion is added.

review.collision_decision: No normalized collision accepted for a new term. Reuse the physical server/client, HTTP software, Jenkins, automation and build process records. Do not import English homonyms as identities.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
